Open hyperlink from email in browser: Use Chrome DevTools Protocol (via Playwright connect_over_cdp) to enumerate open tabs and compare their URLs against expected URLs; use URL normalization/comparison helpers to handle trailing slashes and redirects.
The evaluator checks the ordered list of open tab URLs matches an expected list exactly, so tab order matters; verify both count and URL equality.
Email links may redirect, so compare final resolved URLs rather than raw href values when possible.
Export contacts to CSV: Use compare_csv (line-by-line equality) to verify the exported CSV; the metric is strict by default so field order and header names must match exactly.
Thunderbird exports address book contacts via Tools > Export, producing a CSV with specific column headers; verify the header row and contact rows match a reference file.
Extract email metadata (sender, subject,: Use openpyxl or pandas to load the result xlsx and compare sheet data cell-by-cell against a gold xlsx; the sheet_data rule does DataFrame.equals() after rounding, so string columns must match exactly including whitespace and encoding.

When reading email metadata programmatically (e.g., via Thunderbird profile mbox/maildir or python-based mail parsers), sender_name and sender_address must be split correctly from the From header; CC may be empty string or None and must be stored consistently with the gold file.

Attachment count should reflect the number of MIME parts with Content-Disposition: attachment (or inline parts that are not text/html or text/plain); verify the integer type is preserved in the xlsx cell (not stored as string).
Row ordering matters: emails must be sorted from earliest to most recent by date/time; use the Date header parsed to a datetime for reliable ordering rather than folder sequence.
Column headers in the output sheet must match the gold file exactly (case-sensitive) since DataFrame.equals() compares both index/column labels and values.
Open local HTML file in browser tab: Use Playwright's connect_over_cdp to enumerate open tabs and compare each tab's URL against expected URLs using a URL-normalizing comparator; file:// URLs need exact path matching.
When checking tab sets, order matters — compare full ordered lists of URLs, not just membership.
HTML file structure comparison: Use BeautifulSoup with lxml to parse both HTMLs, then walk recursiveChildGenerator() in parallel, comparing tag names, stripped text content, and attributes; the sdnum attribute (LibreOffice-specific number format) can be safely ignored via an ignore_sdnum option.
Attribute comparison should strip implementation-specific attributes (e.g., sdnum) that vary across export runs but don't affect rendered content.
compare_htmls returns 0.0/1.0 float; a full structural match requires every element pair to match, so even minor attribute differences cause failure unless explicitly ignored.
Add recipients to email To field (compos: Use the accessibility tree to verify recipient address pills in the compose window: look for address-pill elements under MsgHeadersToolbar's To label, each containing a pill-label with the expected email address substring.

CSS selectors on the accessibility tree can target `tool-bar[attr|id=MsgHeadersToolbar]` descendants to find address pills; use `name*=` substring matching to check email addresses without requiring exact display-name formatting.
check_accessibility_tree with selector-based rules returns 0.0 if any required recipient pill is missing, making it suitable for multi-recipient presence checks.
Extract email attachment (PDF) to filesy: Use a binary diff (e.g., shell `diff` or Python filecmp/hashlib) between the extracted file and a reference copy to confirm the attachment was saved correctly and completely.

The `check_list` metric with `unexpect: ['.+']` on a diff output file is the standard pattern: a passing result means the diff file is empty, i.e., the extracted file is byte-identical to the reference.
Append record to spreadsheet (LibreOffic: Use `openpyxl` or `pandas` to load both result and ground-truth xlsx files and compare sheet data with `DataFrame.equals()` after rounding numeric columns; the `compare_table` metric with `sheet_data` rule type is the standard evaluator pattern.
When verifying appended rows, load the first sheet by index (sheet_idx 0) and compare against a ground-truth sheet; row count and cell values must match exactly.
Ensure the file is saved before retrieval — postconfig steps often trigger Ctrl+S via pyautogui; if writing evaluators, account for the file needing to be flushed/closed before reading.
Extract image from email attachment (doc: Use python-docx or similar to parse .docx attachments and extract embedded images; verify image content via SSIM comparison against a reference after resizing both to the same dimensions.
When extracting the 'first' image from a doc, order matters — python-docx exposes inline shapes/relationships in document order; ensure the correct image is selected by index.
Set desktop wallpaper/background image: Use env.controller.get_vm_wallpaper() to retrieve the current wallpaper as bytes, save to a file, then compare with a reference image using SSIM (grayscale, resized to the smaller of the two sizes); a base_score threshold is often used so only meaningful similarity above a baseline counts.

SSIM-based image comparison resizes both images to the minimum of their sizes before comparing — account for resolution differences between the set wallpaper and the reference when writing evaluators.
Empty or None wallpaper bytes indicate the wallpaper was not set; always guard against this before running pixel-level comparisons.
Extract email content (answer key/data): Use openpyxl or pandas to load the result xlsx and compare sheet data cell-by-cell against a gold reference using DataFrame.equals() or sheet_data rule; round numeric values to a fixed precision before comparison to avoid floating-point mismatches.

When verifying tabular scoring data written to a spreadsheet, load both result and expected files with pd.ExcelFile and compare the target sheet by index or name; ensure the sheet index/name mapping is resolved correctly when sheets may be reordered.

For tasks that read structured data from an email (e.g., answer keys in message body or attachment) and write derived values to a spreadsheet, verify the output spreadsheet's cell values rather than intermediate parsing; the compare_table 'sheet_data' rule with openpyxl+pandas is the standard approach.
Remove/delete email account: Account existence is verified by decrypting the Thunderbird profile's stored credentials (using a firefox_decrypt-style tool) and exporting to CSV; check that the removed account's URL+username pair no longer appears in any CSV row

Use csv.DictReader to parse the exported credentials CSV and apply expect/unexpect row-matching logic; an account is considered removed when no row matches both the IMAP server URL and the username fields simultaneously
The profile directory (~/.thunderbird) stores account credentials that persist until explicitly removed; verify removal by checking the decrypted credential store, not just UI state or prefs.js
Add/configure email account (IMAP setup: Use the accessibility tree to verify that account setup fields (display name, email address, password, protocol type) are populated and visible in Thunderbird's account wizard UI.
XPath queries on the accessibility tree can check for presence of text/name attributes containing the email address, display name, password field label, and protocol (IMAP/POP3) simultaneously.
check_accessibility_tree with multiple xpath rules (AND-logic via multiplicative scoring) is effective for confirming multi-field form state without submitting the form.
Protocol selection (IMAP vs POP3) is detectable as a named element or text node in the accessibility tree on the account setup page.
Open about:profiles tab in Thunderbird t: Use the accessibility tree to check for a page-tab element with name 'About Profiles' inside the tabmail-tabs page-tab-list; CSS selectors on the AT XML work well for this (e.g., application[name=Thunderbird] page-tab-list[attr|id='tabmail-tabs']>page-tab[name='About Profiles'])
The check_accessibility_tree evaluator with CSS selectors on AT XML is the right tool for verifying tab presence; no text content check is needed, just element existence
Export/backup inbox emails as individual: Use `ls -R` on the backup directory and apply regex pattern matching against filenames; verify each expected email subject appears as a `.eml` file using `check_list`-style regex rules (subject string + `\.eml` suffix).
The evaluator reads a cached `ls -R` output file and checks each line against expect/unexpect regex patterns — useful pattern for verifying file exports without inspecting file contents.
Email subject strings may contain non-ASCII (e.g., CJK) characters; ensure regex patterns and file reading handle UTF-8 encoding correctly.
Set plain text email signature: Thunderbird stores signature text in prefs.js under keys like mail.identity.idN.htmlSigText; parse prefs.js with a regex matching user_pref("key", value) lines and JSON-decode the value to compare against expected multiline signature content.
Use re.S (DOTALL) flag or equivalent when matching multiline signature strings, since newlines are embedded as \n literals in the JSON-encoded pref value.
Check mail.identity.idN.useremail or related identity keys to confirm the signature is attached to the correct account when multiple identities exist.
Create local mail folder: Local folders appear in the msgFilterRules.dat actionValue as mailbox://nobody@Local%20Folders/<FolderName>; verify folder existence indirectly by checking this URI in filter rules rather than filesystem paths

Local folders in Thunderbird are stored under the Mail/Local Folders directory; verify creation by checking for both a folder file/directory (without .msf extension) and its companion .msf index file using regex patterns on `ls -R` output
Use check_list with expect regex patterns that match the folder name both with and without the .msf suffix to confirm both the mailbox data and index file exist
The .msf file alone is insufficient — confirm the actual folder entry (directory or mbox file) also exists alongside it
Create message filter (subject-based aut: Parse msgFilterRules.dat from the IMAP account directory; each filter block has name/enabled/type/action/actionValue/condition fields — use regex or line-by-line parsing to extract structured filter dicts
Condition strings follow the pattern 'AND (field,operator,value)' — use regex like _condition_pattern.findall() to extract individual condition tuples for comparison
actionValue for move-to-local-folder rules uses URL-encoded mailbox URI: mailbox://nobody@Local%20Folders/<FolderName>
Check both 'enabled' field (yes/no) and 'action' field ('Move to folder') when validating a filter rule
The filter file is located under the IMAP account subdirectory (e.g., ImapMail/<server>/msgFilterRules.dat), not under Local Folders

Parse msgFilterRules.dat line-by-line: lines starting with 'name=', 'enabled=', 'type=', 'action=', 'actionValue=', 'condition=' define each filter; condition= line requires regex extraction of individual condition tokens

Check filter fields: 'enabled' (yes/no), 'action' (e.g. 'Forward', 'Move to folder'), 'actionValue' (destination address or folder URI), 'condition' (list of condition strings or ['ALL'] for match-all)
The dat file is per-account and lives under ImapMail/<server>/ — verify the correct account's dat file when multiple accounts exist
For forward-all filters, condition list should contain 'ALL'; match logic should check subset/presence rather than exact equality to allow extra filters coexisting
Star/flag emails in a mail folder: Thunderbird stores message flags in the global-messages-db.sqlite file; starring a message sets a row in messageAttributes with attributeID=58 and value=1 linked to the message's ID in the messages table — query this table to verify star status rather than inspecting UI state.

Use sqlite3 queries joining messages (folderID) and messageAttributes (attributeID, value) to check that all messages in a target folder have the expected attribute set; aggregate with sum or count to confirm coverage across all messages, not just one.

The folderID in the messages table corresponds to a specific local folder; when writing evaluators, identify the correct folderID for the target folder by inspecting the folderLocations or folders table in the same SQLite database.
Attach file to email (compose window): Use a helper script (like show-thunderbird-attachments.py) that inspects the Thunderbird compose window's attachment list via accessibility tree or DOM; check that the target filename appears in the attachment pane of the correct draft/compose window identified by subject

The evaluator runs the helper script with the draft subject and expected filename as arguments, writing output to a cache file; check_list then regex-matches that output for a success token like 'Attachment added!'
The helper script relies on cssselect or similar libraries to parse Thunderbird's UI state — ensure dependencies are installed before running
Verify the compose window is still open (not sent/closed) as part of the attachment check, since the task requires the draft to remain open
Enable unified/smart inbox (folder tree: Thunderbird stores the active folder-tree view mode in the profile's xulstore.json under the key path ["chrome://messenger/content/messenger.xhtml"]["folderTree"]["mode"]; check that this value matches "smart" to confirm the unified inbox is enabled.
Use check_json with a regex or exact-match rule on the nested key path in xulstore.json rather than inspecting the live UI, since the file is reliably written when the user switches folder modes.
Configure reply quoting settings (auto_q: Parse prefs.js line-by-line with a regex matching `user_pref("key", value)` and use `json.loads` on the captured value group to correctly handle booleans/strings; check keys like `mail.identity.idN.auto_quote`, `mail.identity.idN.reply_on_top`, and related quoting prefs.

The `check_thunderbird_prefs` pattern supports both `expect` and `unexpect` rule sets, so verifiers can assert a pref equals a value OR assert a pref does NOT equal a value — useful when the desired state is the absence/falsehood of a setting.
Enable dark theme/mode (extensions.activ: Parse prefs.js with a regex matching `user_pref("key", value)` lines; check `extensions.activeThemeID` value contains 'dark' (regex match) to confirm a dark theme is active.

Use `check_thunderbird_prefs`-style logic: read prefs.js line-by-line, extract key/value pairs via pattern, then apply method-based matching (exact, regex, etc.) against expected pref keys — this generalises to any Thunderbird preference verification task.
Configure automatic message filters for: Check prefs.js for mail.server.default.applyIncomingFilters=true and mail.imap.use_status_for_biff=false using the check_thunderbird_prefs pattern; parse with a regex matching user_pref("key", value) lines and json.loads the value.
Use unexpect rules to ensure mail.server.default.autosync_offline_stores is not explicitly set to false, since that would disable offline sync needed for subfolder filtering.

The check_thunderbird_prefs evaluator supports both 'expect' and 'unexpect' rule dicts; unexpect passes when the key is absent OR its value does not match the ref, so absence of a key counts as passing the unexpect check.
sender substring validation: Avoid using a broad sender substring that also appears in the subject or other required text, because it can make the sender check pass even when the sender is missing.
vm_file result semantics: vm_file returns a local cached file path; rule code should open or parse that path directly, as this evaluator correctly does for ODT/PDF artifacts.
partial scoring caps: If a required field such as a date is missing, apply any cap after all additive scoring or make the field mandatory; an early cap can be bypassed by later score additions.
vm_command_line file existence: Do not use a vm_command_line rule that ignores stdout/exit status and always returns success. Have the command print explicit machine-readable status, or use vm_file and open the returned local cached path.
plain text exact-line verification: When verifying an output file must have exactly N lines, avoid splitlines-based logic that silently accepts extra trailing blank lines; compare normalized line endings and explicitly reject raw content ending with multiple newlines or containing additional empty records.
draft email verification: Do not concatenate all Drafts contents for email checks; parse the Drafts mbox/MIME messages and require a single draft message to contain the expected recipient, subject, and decoded body to avoid false positives from multiple stale drafts or encoded content.

When using vm_command_line to inspect Thunderbird drafts, do all profile traversal and mbox/maildir parsing inside the VM command and emit stdout/JSON; rule code should not os.walk /home/user/.thunderbird because vm_command_line only returns stdout to the judge.

When verifying Thunderbird drafts, parse the Drafts mbox under /home/user/.thunderbird and check recipient, subject, and decoded body, but make the checks exact enough to reject stale or superficially similar drafts with extra content.
plain text exact line verification: For instructions requiring exactly one line in a plain-text file, compare the full file content allowing at most a single trailing newline rather than filtering non-empty lines or stripping whitespace.
